scale.description: Editorial scores on a shared 1–10 scale for this family's stated priorities. A higher score means a stronger fit; the rationale and evidence remain visible beside every value.

bases.name: Saint-Malo / Dinan
bases.summary: The most balanced first-trip base, combining coast, medieval history, family attractions, food and unusually workable car-free days.
bases.bestFor: A first Brittany trip that needs a bit of everything
compromises: A car still helps for the best day trips

climate.rationale: Cool coastal August conditions with rare extreme heat, tempered by wind and tides.

nature.rationale: Beaches, tidal islands, cliffs and the Rance estuary offer variety, though less wilderness than the western bases.

culture.rationale: Walled Saint-Malo, medieval Dinan, forts and nearby castles form the strongest historical cluster.

familyActivities.rationale: The aquarium, family beaches, ramparts, forts and short day trips work well for a 9–10-year-old in mixed weather.

logistics.rationale: Rail access and walkable centres make this the easiest base to use without a car.

accommodation.rationale: The choice is broad, but August prices near the walls and beach are among the highest in the shortlist.

food.rationale: Seafood, Cancale oysters, markets and abundant crêperies make family meals easy and distinctive.

bases.name: Côte de Granit Rose
bases.summary: The strongest nature-first choice: cool air, remarkable coastal scenery and a rare science-and-outdoors mix for children.
bases.bestFor: Scenery, short walks, wildlife and science activities
compromises: A car makes the coast much easier

climate.rationale: One of the coolest coastal choices, with low heat risk and an exposed, breezy feel.

nature.rationale: Pink granite formations, the GR34, beaches, islands and birdlife are the base's defining strength.

culture.rationale: Lannion and coastal heritage add interest, but the area has a thinner city-and-castle layer than eastern Brittany.

familyActivities.rationale: Parc du Radôme, Cité des Télécoms, the planetarium, boats and manageable coastal walks give strong variety.

logistics.rationale: Lannion provides a rail anchor, but dispersed beaches and viewpoints are substantially easier by car.

accommodation.rationale: Usually below Saint-Malo pricing, although sea-view properties become expensive in peak season.

food.rationale: Markets, crêperies and seafood are reliable, though less concentrated than in Saint-Malo or Morbihan.

bases.name: Brest / Finistère
bases.summary: A cool, good-value western base with excellent science attractions and access to dramatic coast, but less postcard charm.
bases.bestFor: Ocean science, cool weather and western day trips
compromises: A car is needed for the best coast
Wetter and windier than southern Brittany

climate.rationale: The most oceanic option, with the shortlist's lowest heat risk but more wind and rain exposure.

nature.rationale: It opens the door to wild western coasts, islands, Armorique and Crozon, though many highlights are outside the city.

culture.rationale: Maritime heritage is strong, but the rebuilt city offers less medieval character than Saint-Malo or Quimper.

familyActivities.rationale: Océanopolis, the maritime museum and Capucins provide an excellent all-weather family core.

logistics.rationale: Brest works without a car in the city and can be a convenient western gateway, but coastal exploration needs one.

accommodation.rationale: City accommodation is generally better value than the famous coastal resorts.

food.rationale: Seafood and markets are solid, but food is not the main reason the sources recommend Brest.

bases.name: Quimper / South Finistère
bases.summary: A charming and comparatively affordable cultural base for day trips, with beaches and wild coast reached rather than on the doorstep.
bases.bestFor: A walkable historic city with varied coastal day trips
compromises: A car helps for beaches and villages
Slightly warmer than the north and west

climate.rationale: August remains moderate, but inland Quimper is a little warmer than the exposed western and northern coast.

nature.rationale: Excellent coast lies within day-trip range, but nature is not immediately outside the accommodation.

culture.rationale: The historic centre, museums, cathedral and nearby art and fishing towns form a strong cultural circuit.

familyActivities.rationale: Family museum formats and nearby attractions are good, but require more day-trip planning than the leaders.

logistics.rationale: The city has rail access and is walkable, while the beaches and smaller towns are much easier by car.

accommodation.rationale: The research consistently presents Quimper as one of the more affordable bases.

food.rationale: Markets, crêperies, pastry and cider culture fit a relaxed, walkable city stay.

bases.name: Vannes / Carnac / Morbihan
bases.summary: The easiest relaxed-family rhythm, with sheltered water, islands and megaliths, traded against warmer weather and peak-season pressure.
bases.bestFor: Gentler swimming, boats, islands and a slower pace
compromises: Carnac is easier with a car

climate.rationale: Morbihan is warmer and drier, pleasant for water time but less aligned with the family's anti-heat priority.

nature.rationale: The gulf, islands, sheltered bays and nearby peninsula create varied, accessible coastal nature.

culture.rationale: Carnac's megaliths, Vannes and Suscinio give the relaxed beach area substantial historical depth.

familyActivities.rationale: Sheltered beaches, islands, boats, Branféré and adventure activities suit a child particularly well.

logistics.rationale: Vannes is easy to reach and usable without a car; spreading the stay toward Carnac and the gulf benefits from one.

accommodation.rationale: Popular coastal locations carry high August prices and availability pressure.

food.rationale: Markets, oysters, seafood and crêperies are a major part of the area's family appeal.

bases.name: Crozon / Douarnenez
bases.summary: The wildest landscape and freshest coastal feel, best for a family happy to drive and accept fewer easy fallbacks.
bases.bestFor: Wild coast, geology, viewpoints and an outdoors-led stay

climate.rationale: Ocean exposure keeps heat risk very low, with wind and rain as the corresponding trade-off.

nature.rationale: Headlands, cliffs, coves and geology make this the shortlist's most dramatic wilderness base.

culture.rationale: Maritime and fishing heritage adds interest, but culture is secondary to landscape.

familyActivities.rationale: Beaches, boats and outdoor exploration are strong in good weather, with fewer rainy-day anchors.

logistics.rationale: Dispersed sights and limited alternatives make a car effectively essential.

accommodation.rationale: Prices sit between Brest and the most expensive coastal resorts, with fewer urban choices.

food.rationale: Fishing-port food and seafood are attractive, though the choice is less concentrated than in larger bases.
